page.layout: One page of text, running head at top, page number at top left. Line-count numbers in the right margin (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35). Reading order: top paragraph continued from the previous page, then the title, the chapter heading, the text, the Locus heading, and the numbered theses.

main_text.p: na quædam propria Dei & hominum, item versus integros vel mutilatos v. g. partem aliquam exc. 1. euangelij Iohannis, & conantur hoc modo prohibere vel etiam profligare morbos. Sed hic est abusus verbi Dei, quod destinatum est salutianimæ[?], non vero corporis, nisi quatenus illud adhibetur in legitimo usu prædicationis, precationis, & meditationis, ad benedictionem Dei pro salute animæ & corporis impetrandam.5
main_text.head: THEOLOGIA POSITIVA.
main_text.p: Theologia est doctrina reddens hominem sapientem & prudentem ad vitam æternam.15 Estque positiva, vel methodica.

Theologia positiua est ipsissima Scriptura sacra, sic dicta, quòd tradat meras positiones, hoc est, principia firmiter posita. Eiusmodi positiones hinc inde sparsæ sunt in Scripturis, & utiliter ad certa capita siue locos communes revocantur hoc pacto.20
main_text.head: LOCUS I.25
De sacra Scriptura.
main_text.p: 1. Scriptura est θεόπνευστος[?], id est, diuinitus inspirata.
2. Tim. 3. vers. 16. Tota Scriptura diuinitus est inspirata.30
2. Petr. 1. vers. 21. Non voluntate hominis allata est olim prophetia; sed acti a Spiritu sancto locuti sunt sancti Dei homines.
2. Scriptura est lucerna, id est, perspicua, & regula fidei & vitæ.35 Psal. 119.

page.notes: The Greek word after "Scriptura est" is partly garbled in the scan; read as θεόπνευστος with a [?]. The page number is printed as "18б" and read as 186. The catchword and signature are not visible. The right-margin marks read as line-count numbers; the sign in the margin beside "salutianimæ" is uncertain. The word "salutianimæ" is run together in print and kept as printed. The bare reference "Psal. 119." sits at the right of the last paragraph and is kept as a note.
